thesis: The speakers argue that despite rapid technological change in chips and software, the US economy has seen stagnant productivity growth since 1971 due to excessive regulation that prevents the adoption of beneficial technologies like nuclear power, space programs, and faster cars. They posit that the future of the world will run on either American AI or Chinese AI, and that while AI could theoretically drive massive productivity gains, regulatory constraints will likely result in a middle-ground outcome rather than the extremes predicted by optimists or doomsayers.
